title.en: Learn writing craft from fiction: evidence, scene mechanisms and a new-story exercise
title.zh: 怎样拆小说才能学会写：从原文证据、场景机制到自己的新故事

answer.en: A useful fiction analysis explains how a passage changes what a reader knows, expects or sees a character choose. Separate observable details from your interpretation, then state when a technique could work in a different story and when it would fail. A plot summary or a list of praise cannot do that work. Oh Story provides separate short- and long-fiction analysis workflows; analysis-only work is distinct from importing a manuscript for continuation. The original poster-proof example below demonstrates one narrow mechanism and an unsupported reading, then compares two new garden plans with the same facts and outcome but different dramatic emphasis. A separate prose version of Option B shows the uncertain staffing proposal being tested and rejected without recreating the poster scene. It is not a model run, a full-book verdict or evidence of reader demand.
answer.zh: 有用的拆文要说明：一段文字怎样改变读者知道的事、期待的结果，或人物能作的选择。先分开看得见的细节与自己的解释，再说这种手法换到别的故事里，什么条件下成立、什么情况下会失效。剧情复述和一串夸奖代替不了这一步。Oh Story 分别提供短篇与长篇拆文流程；只做分析和导入可续写工程是不同任务。下面用原创海报校样片段示范局部机制与缺乏依据的读法，再比较事实、结局相同而戏剧重心不同的两套菜园方案，并把 B 案写成单独的正文片段，让尚未落实的人手补救在交谈中被提出、被放弃，而不复刻海报场景。这不是模型运行记录、全书结论或读者需求数据。

en: Use text you own or are authorized to use. Keep the source and its location labels available; a synopsis cannot establish exact wording, viewpoint or the placement of a clue. For an excerpt, include the immediate context you actually have and identify what is missing.

Choose a question small enough for the material: how does a hesitation change a negotiation, or why does a reveal change the next action? Distinguish a completed short story, a few chapters from a novel and a single scene. Do not invent an unseen ending to make the analysis complete.

A passage-level reading exercise can stay in ordinary chat. The slash commands below require Oh Story installed in a supported agent host; they are not hosted ZenStory or DSH commands. See [agent skills for writers](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/agent-skills-for-writers) for those boundaries.
zh: 使用自己拥有或获准使用的文本，保留原文与段落位置。梗概不能证明具体措辞、视角或线索出现顺序。只提供片段时，附上实际拥有的相邻上下文，说明哪些部分缺失。
问题要小到材料能够回答，例如一次停顿怎样改变协商，或信息揭示为什么改变下一步行动。区分完整短篇、长篇中的几章和单个场景，不靠编造没读到的结尾补齐分析。
单段精读练习可以只在普通聊天中进行。下述 slash 命令需要在支持的 Agent 宿主中安装 Oh Story，不是 ZenStory 托管版或 DSH 命令；环境区别见[写作者的 Agent Skills 指南](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/agent-skills-for-writers)。

en: Choose analysis, not an accidental import

For analysis-only work, use /story-short-analyze for a complete short piece or /story-long-analyze for a long work. /story-import serves a different goal: building a continuable writing project. The short workflow is a full analysis pipeline, not a command that promises to stop after your favorite paragraph. For the small exercise below, use its ordinary-chat request instead.
Anchor each observation before naming a technique

Record a short quotation or an accurate description with its paragraph or chapter location. Then describe the state before and after: who can act, who knows what, and which condition remains unresolved? “Tense dialogue” names an impression; the unsigned approval box and the promise of a new proof show why printing has not been authorized.
Make the interpretation narrower than the evidence

The poster passage supports a reading in which an omitted credit changes the approval process. It does not establish deliberate theft, a lifelong rivalry or healed trust. Name an alternative explanation when it matters. A plausible reader effect is an interpretation of the text, not a measured response from all readers or a claim about the author’s private intention.
Extract a mechanism with conditions and failure cases

One possible mechanism is that withholding a small, necessary cooperation makes an overlooked contribution consequential. It works here because approval is still needed and the disputed condition can still change. If the printing is already finished, or refusal has no practical effect, the same gesture will not do the same narrative work. A pause elsewhere may simply be hesitation; do not force every scene into this pattern.
Change the conflict, not just the names

Write a new exercise with a different desired outcome, relationship, cost and decision. Keep only the abstract mechanism you chose to practice. The garden example uses an openly stated availability limit and a smaller shared plan, not a hidden credit, a silent signature gesture and a replacement proof. This is a craft exercise, not a legal originality test or a shortcut to copying a passage’s wording. Compare the two garden options by the experience you want: acceptance of a stated limit or release of an unconfirmed workaround. More beats are not automatically better, and a surprise exception would change the agreed story facts. The drafted B passage makes each date change what someone can responsibly propose, then lets the smaller decision take effect; it does not use the source’s unsigned-proof ending again.
Can I study only the first 20 chapters?

You can define a limited reading question, but distinguish it from a documented pipeline checkpoint. The long workflow normally builds the source’s chapter map, analyzes the first three chapters and pauses at 快速预览.md; an explicit full-analysis request continues after that preview. For a first-20-chapter study, label the authorized material as an excerpt and name what you want to learn from that range. A separate ordinary-chat reading brief can stay scoped to that material; it is not a demonstrated “complete first-20 analysis” mode, and twenty chapters are not guaranteed to fit a host’s context. Ask which chapters were actually read and keep any gaps visible. Do not call a novel excerpt a complete short story merely to use the short-analysis workflow.
Can I use staged results before the whole book is analyzed?

For questions about the passages actually covered, yes. That does not make the partial result a complete full-book analysis. For a supplied full novel, Stage 2 targets all indexed chapters, while full-book aggregation and reporting refer to the resulting chapter summaries and outputs. The large-book reference’s 10–20-chapter batches specifically describe Stage 3–5 processing of chapter summaries, not an automatic stop after reading twenty original chapters. Saved partial summaries can inform a question about the passages they actually cover. They do not establish a thousand-chapter novel’s final character arcs, cross-book clue payoffs or ending. Keep a range-limited reading note separate from a claimed complete analysis bundle; the cited contracts do not establish arbitrary-window completion and later seamless merging.
What actually resumes after an interruption?

Resume uses the saved _progress.md, not an agent’s promise to remember. The current contract requires schema_version: 2 and the chapter-boundary table. A paused_after_stage1 checkpoint resumes at Stage 2; other interrupted blocks resume from that block’s starting chapter and overwrite that block’s existing outputs. Preserve author notes separately before a repeat pass. For work that ran with failures, inspect the recorded gaps rather than treating a finished-looking report as complete evidence. A valid checkpoint describes progress on that source; it does not turn independently truncated inputs into one verified full-book reading.
Carry selected lessons into a separate writing decision

Choose which lesson serves your own premise and say what must not transfer: names, plot facts, distinctive props, reveal order or another work’s voice. A practice note is not a completed Oh Story analysis bundle; do not relabel it as one. The documented short-writing flow can read the full analysis bundle, including source text, so do not assume only your abstracted lesson will be used. Set the new story’s boundaries explicitly; the [short-story planning guide](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/short-story-from-idea) helps turn that decision into an independent plan.
zh: 先选只拆文，不误走导入
只要分析时，完整短篇可用 /story-short-analyze，长篇可用 /story-long-analyze。/story-import 的目标不同，是建立可续写的写作工程。短篇拆文是完整分析管道，不是保证只读你最喜欢的一段就停的命令；下面的小练习应采用单独的普通聊天请求。
先定位观察，再给手法命名
记录短引或准确转述，并标明段落、章节位置。随后写清前后状态：谁能行动、谁知道什么、什么条件仍未解决？“对白紧张”只是印象；未签的确认格与重出校样的承诺，才说明为什么印制还没得到确认。
让解释不超出证据
海报片段支持“署名遗漏改变了确认流程”这一读法，却不能证明蓄意侵占、终身宿怨或信任已经修复。必要时列出另一种解释。可能的阅读效果是对文本的理解，不是对所有读者的实测，也不是作者真实意图的证据。
提取机制时，一起写条件与失效情形
一种可选机制是：暂停一项虽小却必需的合作，让被忽略的贡献真正影响下一步。这里成立，是因为确认仍然必要，争议条件也还能修改。如果海报已经印好，或拒绝配合根本没有后果，同一个动作就不承担相同作用。别处的停顿也可能只是犹豫，不能把每场戏都塞进这一模式。
换冲突，不只是换名字

新练习要有不同的目标、关系、代价与决定，只保留选中的抽象机制。菜园练习用公开说明的时间限制和缩小共同计划，替换署名缺失、无声挡住签字与重出校样。这是写作练习，不是法律上的原创判定，也不是沿用原段措辞的捷径。 比较两套菜园方案时，先选想写的体验：接纳明确限制，还是放下尚未成立的补救。节拍更多不自动更好，临时开一个意外例外则会改变已定事实。下方 B 案正文让每个日期都改变人物能提出什么，再把缩小决定落实，不重复原片段里未签校样的结尾。
能不能只研究前20章？

可以限定精读问题，但要与文档中的管道停靠点分开。长篇流程通常先建立原文章节边界表，分析前三章，在 快速预览.md 停靠；一开始明确要求完整拆解时，则保留预览后继续。只想研究前20章，就把有权使用的材料标成节选，说清想从这个范围学什么。另行提出的普通聊天精读请求可以限定在这些材料内，但这不是已经证明存在的“前20章完整拆解模式”，也不保证20章一定装得进宿主上下文。要求说明实际读到了哪些章，缺失保持可见；不要为了改用短篇管道，就把长篇节选叫成完整短篇。
分析未完成，阶段性成果能先用吗？

可以先研究实际覆盖的段落，但局部成果不等于已经完成的全书分析。对提供的完整长篇，Stage 2 的目标是覆盖已索引的全部章节，全书聚合和报告则引用相应摘要与前序产物。大书参考中的10–20章一批，具体指 Stage 3–5 对章节摘要的处理，不是读完20章原文便自动停止的设置。已保存的局部摘要可以帮助回答其实际覆盖段落中的问题，但不能确定千章长篇最终的人物弧、跨卷伏笔回收或结尾。范围有限的精读笔记应与声称完整的拆文资料分开；所引契约没有确立“任意区间完整分析、之后无缝合并”的保证。
中断后，真正接续的是什么？

续跑读取保存的 _progress.md，不靠 Agent 口头说记得。当前契约要求 schema_version: 2 与章节边界表。paused_after_stage1 从 Stage 2 继续；其他分块中断则从该块起始章恢复，并覆盖该块已有产出。重跑前，把作者另加的笔记单独保留。若过程有失败，应查看记录中的缺口，不把外观完整的报告当成完整证据。有效断点说明同一份材料的处理进度，不会把各自截短的输入自动变成一份已确认覆盖全书的阅读。
把选中的收获变成另一项创作决定

决定哪条收获适合自己的梗，并说明不迁移哪些东西：人名、情节事实、独特道具、揭示顺序或另一部作品的声音。练习笔记不是完整的 Oh Story 拆文产物，不要改个文件名就冒充。文档中的短篇写作会读取包括原文在内的整套拆文资料，不能假设它只使用你提炼的抽象方法；新故事边界仍须明确。[短篇规划指南](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/short-story-from-idea)可以帮助把这个决定变成独立设计。

example.en:
ORIGINAL PASSAGE AND READING EXERCISE — written for this guide; not a skill run or a quotation from another work.

The proof:
[P1] At the poster workshop, Lu Qing handed Zhou Mian the final proof. “Once you sign off, I’ll place the order.”
[P2] Zhou pulled a comparison copy from her notebook. Both their handwritten revisions covered it. At the bottom of the new proof, only Lu’s name appeared.
[P3] “Another typo?” Lu asked. Zhou laid her pen across the approval box without signing.
[P4] Lu looked from their revision marks to the credit line. After a pause, Lu changed the credit line to list both names side by side. “I’ll have a fresh proof made like this. You’ll see it before printing.”
[P5] Zhou picked up her pen, wrote “Awaiting new proof” on the back, and left the approval box empty.

Evidence → reading → limit:
• P1 makes Zhou’s approval a stated condition of ordering. P3 and P5 show that approval has not been given. The passage ends with a proposed next step, not an order placed or a poster printed.
• P2 juxtaposes both people’s revision marks with one printed name. Together with P3–P4, that supports reading the credit line as the immediate point of disagreement. It does not tell us who made the omission or whether it was deliberate. A layout oversight is one possible alternative to deliberate exclusion; the passage does not settle the cause.
• P4 offers a visible repair; P5 reserves the final decision until a new proof exists. This can make conditional cooperation legible to a reader. “Zhou forgives years of exploitation” invents both the history and the forgiveness.

Working lesson: a small cooperation can matter when another action genuinely depends on it. Preserve the unmet condition long enough for the response to have a cost or a limit. This is one reading of this scene, not a rule that every ending must withhold approval.

Different-situation exercise — a proposed new design, not facts inferred from the passage:
A community garden wants to plant a second bed. Wen has covered three consecutive Sundays and cannot cover the next one. The proposed expansion assumes Wen will cover that next Sunday too, without anyone having asked. During the meeting, Wen says this directly; nobody discovers a missing name or silently blocks a signature. The group must find another volunteer or leave the second bed unplanted. Design a short scene in which they choose the smaller plan. Give another member a credible reason to want expansion and let Wen care about the garden without promising unavailable time.
What transfers: a contribution previously treated as automatic becomes a real constraint on a shared goal.
What changes: the conflict is future workload rather than credit; the limit is stated aloud; the result is a reduced plan rather than a replacement proof. Do not reuse the original dialogue or its sequence of props and gestures.

TWO AUTHORED SCENE OPTIONS — alternatives for the garden exercise, not consecutive scenes or recorded model outputs.

Shared new design decisions for both options: this meeting is on Wednesday; extra seedlings must be confirmed with the nursery by Thursday for Sunday planting; the nursery cannot hold them without that confirmation. Care for the existing bed is already covered by another volunteer; the second bed needs additional Sunday coverage. Wen is unavailable that whole Sunday. Lin wants the extra bed so two waiting neighbors can join. Qiao might help, but cannot confirm Sunday availability until Friday. These are new story facts chosen for the exercise, not facts recovered from the poster passage. No order for the extra seedlings has been placed.

Option A — make the boundary the turning point:
1. Wen states the Sunday limit at the start. Lin names the disappointment: two neighbors have been waiting, and the expansion would give them space. Both concerns remain legitimate.
2. Lin accepts that there is no confirmed cover in time for the order but asks Wen to explain the smaller plan to the neighbors, thinking a direct explanation will be clearer. Wen agrees to join the conversation, not to describe an unpromised shift as a broken commitment.
3. The group chooses the existing bed only. Lin recognizes that the expansion counted on time nobody had secured and decides to lead the explanation: it was a gap in the group’s plan, not Wen cancelling a promised shift.
4. End with Lin telling the neighbors that the group planned more work than it could staff, so there will be no second bed this Sunday. Wen remains part of the garden without agreeing to cover it. The choice is settled; neither the disappointment nor all future staffing is magically fixed.
Intended emphasis: a clear limit can become part of a shared decision rather than a private refusal. Keep the scene short once that decision is made. The risk is making Lin concede too easily; give the loss of the extra places room in the exchange without turning Lin into a villain.

Option B — let a tempting workaround expose the same constraint:
1. The meeting begins with Qiao’s possible help. Lin suggests reserving the extra seedlings on that basis; Wen then states the Sunday limit. The limit is still explicit, not hidden until a final reveal.
2. Put the two dates in the conversation: the nursery needs Thursday confirmation, while Qiao can answer only on Friday. Qiao does not promise a shift that is still uncertain. In this design the nursery cannot hold the additional seedlings without that confirmation.
3. Wen asks who would actually cover Sunday if Qiao cannot. The group has no confirmed replacement. Rather than rely on Wen or announce a commitment nobody can keep, Lin withdraws the additional seedling request before placing the order.
4. Lin places the order for the existing bed only and gives the neighbors the same smaller-plan update. The tempting solution has been considered and rejected on its conditions, not defeated by an unrelated accident.
Intended emphasis: goodwill and a plausible workaround are not the same as an available contribution. The risk is letting the scene become a calendar explanation; keep each date tied to someone’s proposal, response and choice. If the workaround adds no meaningful conflict to your story, use the shorter option instead.

Choosing between them:
• Choose A if the main movement is whether the group will accept Wen’s stated limit and share responsibility for the disappointment.
• Choose B if the main movement is letting go of a comforting but unconfirmed solution. Its extra exchange earns space only if that hesitation matters for these characters.
• Both preserve the same agreed outcome and Wen’s availability. Do not quietly make Qiao available on Thursday, move the nursery deadline, or have Wen cover “just this once” to produce a tidier ending. A different outcome is possible, but it needs an explicit change to the brief and its consequences, not a covert exception.
• Neither option is a full story or a universal recipe. Keep the one that serves your own characters and desired experience; discard the borrowed mechanism if it pushes your story toward a conflict you do not want.

Ordinary-chat request for this small exercise — no analysis skill invocation:
Read only P1–P5 above. In chat, give three claims with paragraph evidence, one plausible alternative reading and two things the passage does not establish. Do not invent a full story or produce a complete analysis bundle. Then compare the two garden options above against the shared facts and the experience I want to create. Recommend one with a concrete tradeoff, or propose a clearly labeled third option without changing the agreed outcome or borrowing the poster scene’s wording and beat sequence. Mark any additional premise as a decision for me, not an established fact. Do not write files, import a book, start a full-book workflow or draft prose. Stop after the options.

From the chosen lesson to a new passage: Option B in prose
This is original editorial writing for the garden exercise, not analysis evidence, a model output or a scene after Option A. It uses the shared facts above; the dialogue and the meeting's follow-through are proposed prose, not an accepted manuscript. It ends with the smaller plan rather than leaving another approval box waiting to be signed.

“If Qiao can help, we can plant the second bed this week,” Lin said. “Those two neighbors would finally have somewhere to join in.”
“I can only say maybe,” Qiao said. “I won't know until Friday.”
“I can't cover any of Sunday,” Wen said. “The original bed has someone. That doesn't give the second one a person too.”

“The nursery needs confirmation tomorrow. They won't hold the extra seedlings without it.” Lin paused. “What if we order them first?”
“If Qiao can't come after all, who covers it?” Wen asked.
“No one else is confirmed.” Lin looked toward the empty second bed. “I just don't want to make them wait again.”
“I want to help,” Qiao said. “But I can't give you a definite answer tomorrow.”
“Then this week we keep the original bed,” Lin said.

Lin called the nursery and ordered the seedlings for the original bed only.
After the meeting, Lin told the two neighbors, “We're not adding the second bed this week. We planned more work than we have people confirmed to do.”
“So we still have to wait,” one of them said.

What has actually transferred?
The new passage makes unconfirmed labor matter to the plan, but its people do not discover a missing credit or silently obstruct a signature. Qiao's Friday answer cannot support Thursday's commitment; Wen's whole-Sunday limit cannot become the unnamed backup. The dates change the meaning of Lin's “order first” proposal instead of decorating the setting. The existing-bed assignment keeps the choice about expansion, not suddenly abandoning the whole garden.
The consequence is also different. Lin places the smaller order and tells the neighbors, rather than merely promising a revised proof. Their disappointment survives the decision; no promised date for eventual expansion or universal reconciliation appears. Lin's wish to include them remains understandable, just as Wen and Qiao need not become villains for stating what they cannot promise.
If you cut the two-date conflict and leave only “not enough people,” you may be choosing a shorter boundary-focused scene closer to A. That can be a valid creative choice, but it no longer demonstrates why this particular workaround fails. Likewise, making Wen cover the shift changes the selected outcome; it is not simply polishing the ending. The mechanism is useful only if it serves the new story, not because every borrowed pattern must be reproduced.

Optional prose request, separate from the analysis-only request above:
I choose the shared garden facts and Option B. Write a short new passage in this reply: show that Qiao cannot confirm availability until Friday, after the nursery's Thursday deadline, keep Wen unavailable all Sunday, and let Lin order only for the existing bed and explain the smaller plan. Keep the desire to include the neighbors and their possible disappointment. Do not transfer the poster passage's names, wording, distinctive props or sequence of gestures. Do not invent a nursery hold, an earlier answer or a new substitute to rescue the expansion. This is a writing exercise only: no analysis-skill invocation, project-file changes, import or claim that the passage is an accepted manuscript or complete analysis bundle.

A range-limited reading brief — ordinary chat, not a partial-pipeline command:
I am providing only chapters 1–20 of [authorized novel excerpt], not the complete novel. Study how the opening establishes the protagonist’s immediate goal and presents one unanswered question. State which supplied chapters you actually used. Separate observations, possible interpretations and what chapters 21 onward would be needed to establish. If the material is too large to read reliably here, say so and help narrow the question and material. Do not invent the ending, claim full-book coverage, run later analysis stages on my behalf or write files. A useful result is a bounded reading note, not a complete Oh Story analysis bundle.

For example, “this clue is still unresolved within chapters 1–20” may be supported; “the author forgot the clue in the entire novel” is not supported by that range. You can try a newly designed scene based on a local technique without pretending that you have already mapped the reference novel’s whole structure.

For an actual complete short-story analysis in an installed Claude Code workflow, use /story-short-analyze with [the authorized complete text path] and a distinct output location. That invokes the documented full pipeline, not the chat-only exercise. Request analysis only and no subsequent writing or import. Existing analysis under the same title has its own archive/resume/cancel decision; do not silently overwrite it.
example.zh:
原创片段与精读练习——为本指南撰写，不是技能运行记录，也不是引用他人作品。

《校样》：
[P1] 海报工作室里，卢青把最后一版样张递给周眠：“你确认后，我就下单。”
[P2] 周眠从标注本里抽出对照稿，上面留着两人各自的修改笔迹。新样张底部，只有卢青一个人的署名。
[P3] “正文还有错？”卢青问。周眠把笔横放在确认格上，没有签。
[P4] 卢青从两人的修改笔迹看向署名栏，停了一会，把署名改为两人并列：“按这版重出样，印之前再让你看。”
[P5] 周眠拿回笔，在背面写了“待看新样”，把确认格留空。

证据 → 读法 → 边界：
• P1 把周眠确认设为下单条件，P3 与 P5 显示她尚未确认。片段结束时只有下一步的提议，没有下单或印成海报。
• P2 把两人的修改笔迹与单人署名并置，结合 P3–P4，可以把署名看作眼前争议点。但不知道是谁遗漏，也不能判定是否故意。排版疏漏是不同于故意排除的一种可能解释；片段并未确定原因。
• P4 提出可见的修补办法，P5 将最终决定保留到新样张出现后。这能让读者看见有条件的合作。“周眠原谅了多年的剥削”则同时编造了前史与原谅。

暂取的收获：当另一项行动确实依赖合作时，小小的配合也可以改变局面。让尚未满足的条件保持有效，对方的回应才会有代价或边界。这只是本场景的一种读法，不是要求每篇都以暂不确认作结。

不同情境练习——以下是新的设计选项，不是从片段反推的事实：
社区菜园想增种第二块地。温宁已经连续代班三个周日，下周无法再代班。大家提出扩种时，仍把温宁下周代班算作已有的人手，尚未问过她。会上，温宁直接说清这件事；没有人发现漏掉的署名，也没有人默默拦住签字。大家必须另找志愿者，或暂时不种第二块地。设计一场最终选择缩小计划的短戏：让另一位成员有可信的扩种理由，也让温宁在关心菜园的同时，不承诺自己拿不出的时间。
迁移的是：原本被当成理所当然的投入，成为共同目标必须面对的实际限制。
改变的是：争议从署名转为未来分工；限制直接说出；结算是缩小计划，而非更换校样。不沿用原对白或那串道具、动作顺序。

两套作者自拟的场景方案——用于上面的菜园练习，二选一，不是连续两场，也不是模型运行输出。

两案共同确认的新设计：会议在周三；要在周日增种，必须于周四向苗圃确认追加苗木，苗圃无法在未确认的情况下保留这批苗。原有菜地的照料已由另一名志愿者承接，第二块地需要额外的周日人手。温宁整个周日都无法值守。林澄希望扩种，让两位等候的邻居也能参与。乔越可能帮忙，但要到周五才能确认周日是否有空。以上都是本练习新定的故事事实，不是从海报片段中还原的内容。追加苗木尚未下单。

方案 A——把接纳边界作为转折：
1. 温宁一开场便说清周日无法值守。林澄说出缩小计划的损失：两位邻居已经等了一阵，扩种才有他们的位置。双方在意的事都有理由。
2. 林澄接受下单前没有确定替班人的事实，却请温宁向邻居说明缩小计划，觉得本人解释更清楚。温宁愿意一起去谈，但不把从未答应的班次说成自己违约。
3. 大家选择只种原有菜地。林澄意识到扩种方案用了尚未落实的人手，决定由自己先说明：问题是共同计划的缺口，不是温宁取消了已承诺的班次。
4. 收在林澄告知邻居：大家规划的工作超过了能落实的人手，本周日不增种第二块地。温宁仍参与菜园，但没有答应值守。选择已定，失望与未来所有排班并没有一起消失。
想突出的是：明确的个人限制怎样进入共同决定，而不只停留在一次私人拒绝。决定之后不必拖长。风险在于林澄让步过快；给少了两个参与名额的损失留一点回应空间，但不把林澄写成反派。

方案 B——让看似可行的补救暴露同一限制：
1. 会议先讨论乔越可能帮忙。林澄据此提议预订追加苗木，温宁随后说清周日无法值守。限制仍然明说，不藏到最后才揭晓。
2. 把两个日期带进对话：苗圃周四要确认，乔越周五才能答复。乔越不把尚未确定的时间说成已承诺的班次。本设计中，苗圃也不能在未确认的情况下保留追加苗木。
3. 温宁问，如果乔越最终来不了，周日究竟由谁值守？大家没有确定的替代者。林澄不再押注温宁，也不宣布没人能承担的承诺，而是在下单前撤去追加苗木的请求。
4. 林澄只为原有菜地下单，并向邻居说明同样的缩小计划。看似可行的办法是在自身条件下被考虑、被放弃，不是被临时塞入的事故打断。
想突出的是：善意和听上去可行的办法，不等于真实可用的投入。风险在于写成日历讲解；每个日期都应牵动某人的提议、回应与选择。如果这次补救并未给自己的故事增加有意义的冲突，就用较短的方案。

怎样选：
• 核心变化若是大家是否接纳温宁说清的限制、共同承担解释失望的责任，可选 A。
• 核心变化若是放下一个让人安心却尚未成立的办法，可选 B。多出来的交锋，要对这些人物的犹豫有用才值得保留。
• 两案保留同一个已定结果和温宁的时间边界。不为收得漂亮就悄悄让乔越周四有空、挪后苗圃期限，或让温宁“就再顶这一次”。可以另选结果，但要明确修改创作要求并承担后果，不靠暗中开例外。
• 两案都不是完整故事或通用公式。保留服务自己人物与目标体验的那一案；如果借来的机制把故事推向了不想写的冲突，就放弃这个机制。

适用于本小练习的普通聊天请求——不调用拆文技能：
只读上面的 P1–P5。在聊天中给出三条带段落依据的判断、一种合理的替代读法，以及两件文本尚不能证明的事。不补全整篇故事，不生成完整拆文资料。再依据共同事实与我想写的体验，比较上面两案，带着具体取舍推荐其中一案；也可明确标注第三种设计，但不改变已定结果，不借用海报片段的措辞或情节节拍。进一步新增的前提标为需要我决定的内容，不当成已成立事实。不写文件、不导入书、不启动全书流程、不写正文。列出方案后停止。

从选定收获到新段落：把 B 案写成正文
这是为菜园练习写的原创编辑示例，不是拆文证据、模型输出，也不是接在 A 案之后的另一场。沿用上方共同事实；对白与会议后的落实是本版写法，不是已经采纳的书稿。这里收在缩小计划，不再留一个确认格等人签字。

“乔越要是能帮忙，第二块地这周就能种。”林澄说，“那两位邻居总算有地方了。”
“我还只能说可能。”乔越说，“周五才能定。”
“我这周日整天都不能值守。”温宁说，“原来的菜地有人接，不等于第二块也有人。”

“苗圃明天就要确认。不确认，他们不会留这批追加苗。”林澄顿了顿，“要不先订下来？”
“如果乔越最后来不了，谁值守？”温宁问。
“还没找到能定下来的。”林澄看向空着的第二块地，“我就是不想再让他们等。”
“我想去，”乔越说，“可明天我给不了准话。”
“那这周就先种原来的。”林澄说。

林澄给苗圃打电话，只订原有菜地需要的苗木。
会后，林澄向那两位邻居说明：“这周不增种第二块了。我们排出来的活，比能落实的人手多。”
“还得等啊。”其中一人说。

真正迁移了什么？
新段落让未落实的劳动影响计划，但没有人发现缺失署名，也没有人无声挡住签字。乔越周五的答复，接不上周四的承诺；温宁整个周日的限制，也不能变成默认兜底。日期改变了“先订下来”这项提议意味着什么，不只是摆在背景里。原菜地已有人照料，选择针对扩种，不突然变成放弃整个菜园。
后果也不同：林澄实际订下较小范围，并告诉邻居，不只承诺再改一张校样。失望仍在，没有凭空给出下次扩种日期，也没有让大家立刻和气满意。林澄想让邻居参与的理由仍可理解；温宁和乔越说明不能承诺的事，也不必因此成反派。
若删去两个日期的冲突，只剩一句“人手不够”，可以是在另选更接近 A 的简短边界场景；这个选择并非无效，却不再演示眼前这项补救为什么行不通。让温宁最后顶班，同样改了已选结果，不是只把结尾润得漂亮。只有适合自己的新故事，这项机制才值得留，不为完成迁移练习硬复现模式。

可选的正文请求——与上方只做分析的请求分开：
我选菜园共同事实与 B 案，只在本次回复写一个新短段：写清乔越周五才能确定能否帮忙，苗圃却在周四要确认；保留温宁整个周日不能值守，让林澄只为原菜地下单，并解释缩小计划。保留想让邻居加入的理由，以及对方可能的失望。不搬用海报片段的人名、措辞、独特道具与动作顺序，不新增苗圃留苗、提前答复或临时替班来救回扩种。这只是写作练习：不调用拆文技能、不修改项目文件、不导入，也不声称片段已成为书稿或完整拆文资料。

范围有限的精读请求——普通聊天，不是启用局部管道的命令：
我只提供 [有权使用的小说节选] 第1–20章，不是完整小说。请研究开篇怎样建立主角的眼前目标，以及怎样呈现一个尚待解答的问题。说明实际用到了哪些提供的章节，分开观察、可能的读法，以及必须读到第21章以后才能确定的事项。若材料大到无法在这里可靠读完，请说明并帮我收窄问题与材料。不补结尾、不声称覆盖全书、不替我启动后续分析阶段、不写文件。我要一份范围明确的阅读笔记，不是完整的 Oh Story 拆文资料。

例如，“这条线索在第1–20章内尚未解答”可能有依据；“作者在整部小说里忘了这条线索”则不能只凭这个范围判断。可以把局部手法用于另行设计的场景，但不用假装自己已经掌握了对标小说的全书结构。

如果实际要在已安装的 Claude Code 环境中完整拆一篇短篇，可用 /story-short-analyze，提供 [有权使用的完整原文路径] 和独立输出位置。这会进入文档规定的完整管道，不是上面的聊天小练习。明确只做分析，不继续写作或导入。同名已有拆文还有归档、续跑或取消的选择，不应静默覆盖。

en: For the analysis and comparison exercise: located observations, bounded interpretations and new design options. A separately requested practice passage is writing, not new evidence about the source, an accepted manuscript or a complete Oh Story analysis bundle.

For the documented complete short workflow: 拆文库/{书名}/ contains 原文/, 拆文报告.md, 情节节点.md, 写作手法.md and _meta.json, unless an alternative output location was requested. These files have distinct roles; preserve the original material.

For the long workflow’s opening stop: 快速预览.md and first-three-chapter analysis material, with later stages still pending unless requested and completed. For a range-limited reading note, state the actual chapter range, source and unresolved questions; that note is an editorial aid, not a replacement output contract. Analysis-only delivery is not a continuable project with new chapters and tracking.
zh: 分析与比较练习产出：可定位的观察、有边界的解释，以及新的设计选项。另行请求的练笔段落属于写作，不是关于原文的新证据、已采纳书稿或完整 Oh Story 拆文资料。
文档中的完整短篇管道产出：默认 拆文库/{书名}/ 下的 原文/、拆文报告.md、情节节点.md、写作手法.md 与 _meta.json；另行指定位置则使用该位置。文件各有职责，应保留原始材料。
长篇开篇停靠产出：快速预览.md 及前三章分析材料；后续阶段除非已被要求并完成，否则仍未完成。另做范围有限的精读笔记时，应说明实际章段、材料来源和未决问题；它是编辑辅助，不是替代输出契约。只做拆文，不等于建立了带后续章节与追踪的可续写工程。

en: Can another reader find the detail behind each important claim? Mark absent facts as not established instead of inferring them from genre expectations. Keep the original passage separate from your suggested improvements.

Does the new exercise have its own conflict, costs and outcome, or merely substitute names and objects? State a case where the selected mechanism would fail. If it does not serve your story, discard it rather than force the story to match.

Separate text coverage, file completion and literary judgment. An opening preview, structured report or automatic check cannot establish market popularity, universal reader response or that your new story will succeed.
zh: 另一位读者能否找到每个重要判断的依据？没有的事实写“尚不能确定”，不按题材预期补齐。原文与自己提出的改法应保持分开。
新练习有自己的冲突、代价与结果，还是只替换名字和道具？写出所选机制的一种失效情形。如果它不服务自己的故事，就放弃，不让故事倒过来适应它。
分开文本覆盖、文件完成与文学判断。开篇预览、结构化报告或自动检查，都不能证明市场热度、所有读者的反应或新作品必然成功。

title.en: AI character profiles feel flat? Turn motives into story choices
title.zh: AI 生成人设很完整，人物却不行动？把目标、动机与选择连起来

answer.en: A detailed character profile does not yet explain why someone acts. Give the character a concrete goal, a reason it matters to them, an obstacle and something they could lose; then show how their usual way of solving problems shapes a choice. Oh Story’s character references distinguish goals from motives and connect motivation to cause, intention, constraint and risk. The original fantasy-courier example below turns “proud but responsible” into a sequence of decisions. A separate prose excerpt then lets the offer, resistance and agreement happen in dialogue and action. These are original editorial examples, not a model run or a requirement that every character needs trauma, a hidden secret or a growth arc.
answer.zh: 完整人设表还不能解释一个人为什么行动。先给人物具体目标、在乎这个目标的理由、眼前阻碍与可能失去的东西，再看他惯用的解决办法如何影响一次选择。Oh Story 的角色参考区分目标与动机，并用起因、意图、约束和风险梳理动机链。下面的原创奇幻信使示例把“骄傲但负责”变成连续的决定。再用一段单独的正文示例，让提议、抵抗和约定真正发生在对白与动作里。这些是原创编辑示例，不是模型生成实录，也不要求每个人物都有创伤、隐藏秘密或成长弧线。

en: One character, a specific situation and the facts you have already approved. For an existing manuscript, bring the relevant scene and character notes you own or are authorized to use; do not replace established history with a fresh profile.

Decide whether you want alternatives in chat, a saved character design or a prose revision. This exercise can stay in chat; using it in an Oh Story book project requires a configured supported host. The [writer’s skill guide](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/agent-skills-for-writers) separates discussion, planning files and the later prose request.
zh: 一个人物、一件具体处境，以及已经确认的事实。已有小说应带上你拥有或获准使用的相关场景与角色材料，不用新生成的人设覆盖已经成立的前史。
先分清这次要聊天里的候选方案、保存角色设计，还是修改正文。本练习可以只在聊天里讨论；用于 Oh Story 书稿项目时，需要已配置的受支持宿主。[作者 Skill 指南](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/agent-skills-for-writers)区分了讨论、规划落盘与后续正文请求。

en: Separate the goal from the reason it matters

“Deliver the beacon wick before dusk” is a result to pursue. “Have my route judgment recognized, rather than be seen only as someone who follows instructions” explains why this delivery matters to this character. Separate the immediate task from the longer ambition. A motive can involve care, belonging, curiosity or responsibility; it need not be revenge or a secret wound. The bundled web-fiction template favors personally meaningful motives, not a universal theory of human behavior.
Turn a trait into a habitual tactic

A useful question is not only “Is this person proud?” but “What do they do when someone offers help?” In the example, skill at reading wind has made independent route-finding a successful habit; treating every contribution as a denial of that skill is where the habit becomes a liability. If you designate something a weakness, show where it causes a mistake or narrows a useful option. Do not invent incompetence in an established strength simply to force a lesson.
Put a real obstacle between the habit and the goal

Use the situation’s approved limits. Here the direct route is closed and a viable relay exists, but taking it means giving up a solo delivery. List what each available choice preserves and gives up. A difficult choice need not threaten a life: losing time, recognition or a valued opportunity can matter. Do not add a new power, an arbitrary accident or a villain solely to make the card’s adjectives visible.
Give the other person an independent move

The relay partner also wants the beacon lit, but will not help conceal who flew which leg. She prepares the south-route wings and proposes a handoff instead of waiting to approve the protagonist’s idea. Her action creates an option and her boundary changes its terms. The character reference explicitly gives supporting and allied characters their own actions and motives; disagreement does not automatically make someone an antagonist.
Make a change of action legible

Show the offer, the first response, what the character learns or notices, and the revised choice. One new fact may justify a changed tactic without changing the underlying motive. Here recognition still matters after the courier accepts a relay; he chooses the route and accepts responsibility rather than pretending help never happened. That is more specific than declaring that he has suddenly become humble, and it does not erase the partner’s contribution. In prose, give the resistance room to appear before the agreement. The excerpt below keeps the desire for recognition alive instead of replacing the decision with an announcement of growth.
Choose growth or a tested conviction, not a compulsory cure

A growth story needs an event and response that make the change credible. A character can also hold a considered belief while circumstances reveal its strength, limits or cost. Oh Story’s reference explicitly permits stable protagonists; it does not require every scene to improve them. For the courier below, a single relay can revise one decision without curing a lifelong habit. Do not retrofit childhood trauma to explain every preference, or mistake a new action for a new personality.
Before fixing “out of character,” identify the actual mismatch

A statement that contradicts established history, a character’s disputed claim and a changed tactic under different conditions need different editorial responses. Compare the passage with the relevant earlier scene and ask who is speaking, what that person knows and what has changed. A character can conceal or misrepresent something; that possibility does not automatically prove intentional deception or excuse a writing error. Nor does accepting help once require accepting every later offer. Oh Story’s review reference checks both unsupported motive changes and actions that conflict with characterization; the distinctions here are a reading aid, not a new automatic verdict or rubric.
Save approved design separately from events that happened

Treat proposed motives, secrets and future turning points as choices for the author. In a long-form project, static design belongs in `设定/角色/{角色名}.md`; chapter-current state is tracked separately. A planned acceptance of help is not a completed event. Preserve existing decisions, identify the affected outline range and use [outline to chapter](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-to-chapter) for the next planning step. When the problem is already-written behavior, use the [review-to-revision guide](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/review-and-revise) to agree on scope before rewriting.
zh: 把要做到什么，与为什么在乎分开
“天黑前送到信标灯芯”是要实现的结果；“让别人认可自己的航路判断，而不只是把自己当执行指令的学徒”，才说明这趟任务为什么对这个人重要。把眼前任务与更长远的志向分开。动机可以关乎照顾、归属、好奇或责任，不必总是复仇或秘密伤口。随包网文模板强调对人物切身重要的理由，不是一套适用于所有人的心理学定律。
把性格词换成惯用办法
不只问“他骄傲吗”，而要问“别人提出帮助时，他会怎么做”。示例中，读风能力让独自判断航路成为有效习惯；把任何人的参与都当成否定自己的能力，才使这个习惯变成问题。如果把某项写成弱点，就展示它在哪里导致错误或缩窄了有用选项。不要为了上成长课，临时把已经成立的强项写成无能。
让真实阻碍卡住惯用办法
使用处境里已经确认的限制。本例直达航路封闭，中继可行，但选择中继就不能再把它称作独自送达。列出每个可行选择保住什么、放弃什么。重要选择不必都危及生命，时间、认可或一次珍惜的机会也可以有分量。不为展示人设标签，临时添加新能力、任意事故或反派。
让对手戏人物先作自己的行动
中继搭档也想让灯塔亮起来，但不愿帮忙隐瞒各人飞了哪一段。她准备南线滑翔翼、提出交接办法，不是站着等主角的点子。她的行动创造一个选项，她的底线改变合作条件。角色参考明确要求配角和同阵营人物也有自己的行动与动机；持有不同意见，不自动等于反派。
让改主意有可见的来路
写出提议、第一反应、人物得知或注意到的内容，以及后来的选择。新信息可以解释策略改变，不必把底层动机一起换掉。这里信使接受中继后，仍然在乎认可；他选择航路、承担责任，而不是假装别人没帮过忙。这比宣布“他突然学会谦虚”更具体，也不抹去搭档的贡献。写成正文时，要让抵抗先于答应出现。下方片段保留他仍想被认可的念头，不用一句成长宣言替人物完成决定。
可以成长，也可以让坚定信念接受考验
成长故事需要事件与回应，让变化有来路；人物也可以坚持经过考虑的信念，让处境显出它的力量、局限或代价。Oh Story 的参考明确允许稳定型主角，不要求每一场戏都把人改好。下面的信使可以只在这次中继里修改一个决定，不必就此治好长期习惯。不要用补一段童年创伤来解释所有偏好，也不要把换一个做法直接当成换了整个人。
修“崩人设”前，先判断到底哪里不一致
一句违背既定前史的陈述、角色有争议的说法，以及处境变化后的策略调整，需要不同的编辑处理。把当前段落与相关旧场景并读，问是谁在说、此人知道什么、条件改变了什么。角色可能隐瞒或歪曲，但“可能”不证明作者有意设计了欺骗，也不能自动替笔误开脱；接受过一次帮助，更不等于往后每次都必须接受。Oh Story 审稿参考同时检查无铺垫的动机转变与不合人设的行动；这里的区分是阅读辅助，不是新增自动裁决或评分规则。
批准的人设与已经发生的事分开保存

候选动机、秘密和未来转折都先交作者选择。长篇项目中，静态设计放在 `设定/角色/{角色名}.md`，截至当前章的状态另作追踪；计划接受帮助，不等于已经发生。保留已有裁定，点名受影响的细纲范围，再用[从章纲到章节](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/outline-to-chapter)继续规划。若问题已出现在正文里，先按[审稿到改稿指南](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/review-and-revise)约定范围，再动笔重写。

example.en:
Original planning example — The South-Route Relay. Written for this guide, not an Oh Story run or a complete scene.

Approved fictional facts:
Ali is an apprentice glider courier, good at reading wind. He wants his route judgment recognized and often treats assistance as evidence that others do not trust it. He has volunteered to deliver a new wick to the ridge beacon before dusk. The north route is closed today; no one may fly it. The south route is open. Ali alone cannot complete it before dusk, but a two-person relay can. Nanzhi can take the first leg while Ali uses a separate launch point for the second. Both know these conditions; no hidden weather discovery is needed. If they defer until morning, the beacon will stay unlit tonight. No additional disaster is established.

Nanzhi's position:
She wants the beacon working and wants the relay honestly acknowledged. She has prepared the south-route wings and proposes the handoff. She will fly her leg, but will not pretend Ali delivered the whole route alone. The story has not promised a promotion for either of them.

A profile that has not yet become a plot:
“Ali is proud but responsible. When the north route closes, he understands the value of teamwork, accepts help and grows.”
This skips his resistance and the decision; adding another paragraph of biography would not supply them.

One possible sequence, not an approved new chapter:
1. Nanzhi lays out the two departure points and offers the first leg. Ali asks whether the relay can still be called his solo delivery. His concern becomes observable rather than merely labeled “pride.”
2. She refuses to hide her contribution. The route remains available; what is unavailable is both using her help and claiming he worked alone.
3. Ali looks again at the wick and the two prepared wings. No new secret arrives. He has to choose between tonight's delivery with shared credit and preserving the hope of a later solo delivery while leaving the beacon dark tonight.
4. He asks Nanzhi to take the first leg, chooses the agreed second-leg launch point and says he will describe the relay as a relay. He has not stopped wanting recognition; he accepts that today's sound route judgment includes someone else's work.
5. End the planning beat with the handoff agreed and both preparing to depart. Delivery has not happened yet. A later scene must establish arrival before the beacon can be recorded as lit.

What this version does not claim:
Ali is not now humble forever; Nanzhi has not forgiven an invented earlier betrayal; teamwork does not guarantee promotion. The north route does not become safe through courage. If you want a different outcome, change the design explicitly instead of smuggling it into a character card.

From the plan to prose: one proposed scene excerpt
This original passage realizes the candidate relay agreement above. It is not an accepted chapter, a later event or an Oh Story output. Close third person stays with Ali; the gestures and phrasing are proposed staging, not additional route facts. Neither courier takes off in this excerpt.

“I fly the first leg,” Nanzhi said. “You take over from the second launch point.” She held out her hand.
Ali kept one hand on the wick. There was nothing wrong with the arrangement.
“And when they ask at the beacon who delivered it?”
“We did.”
“I fly the last leg.”
“And I fly the first.” Nanzhi drew her hand back and stood beside the prepared wing. “I'll do my part. Don't call a relay a solo delivery.”
He looked down at the wick beneath his palm. The north route was closed; alone on the south route, he would be too late. She had told him nothing he didn't know. Waiting until morning would leave the beacon dark tonight.
He had wanted a route they would call his. The relay that could get it there tonight still needed both of them.
“Then we relay.” Ali passed her the wick. “You take the first leg. I'll go to the second launch point. If they ask, we say we both did it.”
“And which leg each of us flew,” she said, taking it.
“All right.”
He reached for a line on his own wing. Saying “we” still tightened his chest; he did not add “mostly me.”

What makes this more than a profile recap?
• Ali tries to keep the solo claim before accepting the offer. His questions put his wish for recognition into the exchange without making him unable to read a route. The internal passage stays with the dilemma he already knows; it uncovers no convenient secret.
• Nanzhi offers a workable contribution and insists it remain visible. Her reply is about what she will do and how it will be described, not a lecture that exists only to improve him. Sharing the delivery goal does not give them identical aims in this conversation.
• The turn is specific: he passes over the wick and agrees to name both contributions. Reluctance remains. This is not a permanent cure, a promotion, or evidence that the beacon has been lit; the launch-point transfer and both flights still lie ahead.
The scene chooses internal access as well as dialogue. A more external telling is possible, but would need its own readable resistance and decision; it should not simply delete the difficult beat and keep “All right.” Nor must every gesture be repeated in a full chapter after it has done its work.

A prose-only request after selecting this direction:
Using the approved relay facts and outcome, write one short close-third-person passage from Ali's viewpoint in this reply. Keep his attempt to claim the delivery alone, Nanzhi's independent contribution and boundary, and his eventual agreement to describe the relay honestly. Stop before either launch. Do not import a new route, weather discovery or future reward to settle the choice. Keep Nanzhi's private thoughts outside the viewpoint. This is a scene proposal only: no project-file changes, writing-skill run or chapter-state updates, and not a complete chapter.
To use the chosen version in a book, request the relevant outline and prose work explicitly; this chat excerpt does not become accepted manuscript history on its own.

Three different continuity questions — independent hypothetical review exercises, not new events in the planned relay above:
For these exercises only, suppose the author has actually written Ali agreeing to the relay and acknowledging Nanzhi's part. This premise does not establish that either flight or delivery has happened.

1. A factual contradiction:
A later passage, explicitly using reliable neutral narration, says: “Ali had never agreed to share a task with anyone.” That conflicts with the written agreement. Correct or qualify the line within the authorized edit scope; do not erase the earlier agreement or invent amnesia to defend it. If the book intentionally uses unreliable narration, establish that separate design and its textual signals before treating this as the same case.

2. A line whose purpose is unresolved:
Ali tells another person, “I've never agreed to share a task with anyone.” The claim conflicts with the agreement, but it is now his speech. It might be bluster, deception or a draft inconsistency; the isolated line does not settle which. Ask what he wants from this listener and how the scene frames or answers the claim. Keep “Ali said X” separate from “X is true.” Do not invent a secret motive, automatically normalize the line into truthful speech or declare it successful subtext without supporting material.

3. A changed tactic, not necessarily a changed character:
For a separate later assignment, the author explicitly establishes that Ali can take an open route alone and still arrive on time. He chooses to go alone. That choice need not undo his earlier willingness to relay: the obstacle is different, while recognition and independent judgment can still matter to him. This new assignment does not reopen the north route in the earlier scene. If the intention is a deeper change in values instead, ask what events and responses support it rather than treating either solo work or cooperation as a permanent personality test.

For an existing manuscript, request the narrowest supported finding: quote the relevant passage and earlier basis, distinguish fact from interpretation, then say whether a local correction, a clearer scene transition or an author decision is needed. A finding is not authorization to rewrite the character or the later chapters.

Ordinary chat request before saving anything:
Using only the approved facts above, discuss Ali's immediate goal, personal motive, usual tactic and the choice he faces. Identify the passages that support each inference; leave missing history unknown. Keep Nanzhi's separate motive and contribution. For this comparison, keep the proposed ending where both agree to the relay; offer one alternative sequence and explain what it emphasizes differently. Do not add trauma, secret powers, a promotion or a completed delivery.
Reply here only; do not start a writing skill or create or edit files. This is a requested scope, not a guaranteed tool-access restriction.

After selecting a design, explicitly request the relevant character/outline updates. Ask for prose separately.
example.zh:
原创规划示例——《南线中继》。为本指南撰写，不是 Oh Story 运行记录，也不是完整场景。

已确认的虚构事实：
阿砾是擅长读风的滑翔信使学徒。他想让自己的航路判断被认可，常把他人协助理解成对这种能力的不信任。他主动接下任务，要在天黑前把新灯芯送到山脊信标灯塔。北线今天封航，谁都不能飞；南线开放。阿砾独自走南线赶不及天黑前送达，两人中继可以。南枝能飞第一段，阿砾从另一处起飞点接第二段。两人都知道这些条件，不需要临时发现隐藏天气信息。如果延至明晨，灯塔今晚就不会亮；并未约定另有灾难。

南枝自己的立场：
她想让灯塔工作，也希望中继得到如实承认。她已准备好南线滑翔翼，并提出交接办法。她愿意飞自己的一段，但不愿装作整条路都是阿砾独自完成。故事没有承诺任何一人因此晋升。

还没变成情节的人设摘要：
“阿砾骄傲但负责。北线封航后，他明白团结的重要，接受帮助，获得成长。”
这里跳过了抵抗和决定，再加一段人物生平，也补不出它们。

一种候选推进，不是新章既定事实：
1. 南枝摆出两个起飞点，提出自己飞第一段。阿砾问，中继还能算他独自送达吗？在乎的东西变得可见，不只是贴着“骄傲”标签。
2. 她拒绝隐去自己的贡献。航路仍然可用；不能同时得到的，是使用她的帮助，却声称自己独自完成。
3. 阿砾重新看向灯芯和备好的两只滑翔翼。没有新秘密降临。他必须在今晚共同完成并分享功劳，与保留今后独自完成的希望、让灯塔今夜不亮之间选择。
4. 他请南枝飞第一段，选定约好的第二段起飞点，并说明会把中继如实说成中继。他没有突然不在乎认可，而是接受这次可靠的航路判断包含别人的工作。
5. 这段规划停在交接约定落定、两人准备出发。送达还没发生；后续场景真正写到抵达，才能把信标灯记作已亮。

这版没有声称：
阿砾从此永远谦虚；南枝原谅了一场杜撰的旧日背叛；合作必定换来晋升。勇气不会把封航的北线变安全。若想换结局，应明确改设计，而不是藏进角色卡。

从规划到正文：一种场景片段
以下原创片段把上面的中继约定写出来，不是已采纳章节、后续新事件或 Oh Story 输出。第三人称限知贴近阿砾；手势和措辞是本版调度，不是额外航路条件。两人都尚未起飞。

“第一段我飞，”南枝说，“你在第二个起飞点接。”她伸出手。
阿砾一只手按着灯芯。这个安排没有问题。
“到灯塔，问是谁送的呢？”
“我们。”
“最后一段是我飞。”
“第一段是我。”南枝收回手，站在备好的滑翔翼旁，“我飞我的那段。别把中继说成你独自送达。”
他低头看着掌下的灯芯。北线封航，独自走南线又赶不上；她没说出什么他不知道的事。拖到明早，今晚灯塔就不会亮。
他想要一条能被叫作自己的航路。可今晚要把灯芯送到，仍少不了他们两个人。
“按中继走。”阿砾把灯芯递过去，“第一段交给你。我去第二个起飞点接。问起来，就说我们两个。”
“各自飞哪一段，也照实说。”南枝接过灯芯。
“好。”
他的手伸向自己翼架上的系绳。说成“我们”仍让他胸口发紧，嘴里却没再补上“主要是我”。

为什么这不只是把人设复述一遍？
• 阿砾先争取独自送达的说法，再接受帮助。追问让他在乎认可这件事进入交谈，却没把他写成不会判断航路；内心段落处理的是他早已知道的难题，不靠突然发现秘密开路。
• 南枝提出可行贡献，也坚持它不能被抹掉。她说自己肯做什么、怎样如实讲述，不是专为教育主角发表演说。两人都想送到，不等于这场谈话想争取的东西完全相同。
• 转折落在具体行动：他交出灯芯，同意把两人的贡献说清，不情愿却仍在。这不是性格从此治好、获得晋升，更不是灯塔已经亮起；到另一处起飞点交接与两段飞行还在后面。
本版同时采用内心与对白。也可以选更外在的叙述，但仍要让抵抗和决定可读，不能删掉难处只留下一个“好”；进入完整章节时，已经完成作用的动作也不必机械重复。

选定这个方向后，可单独请求一段正文：
只按已确认的中继事实与结尾，在本次回复写一段贴近阿砾的第三人称限知短场景。保留他争独自功劳的尝试、南枝自己的贡献与底线，以及他最后答应如实承认中继。停在两人起飞前，不用新航路、天气发现或将来奖励替他解决选择，不越出视角代写南枝私下的想法。这里只是场景提案：不修改项目文件，不启动写作 skill，不更新章节状态，也不是完整一章。
要把选定版本用于书稿，再明确请求相应细纲和正文工作；聊天里的这一段不会自行变成已经采纳的章节事实。

三种不同的连续性问题——独立的假设审读练习，不是把上面尚未成文的中继当成新发生事件：
仅为这些练习另作前提：作者后来确实写出了阿砾答应中继，并承认南枝参与分工。这个前提不表示起飞或送达已经发生。

1. 事实矛盾：
后文明确采用可靠、中性的叙述，却说：“阿砾从来没答应过与任何人分担任务。”这与已经写出的约定冲突。应在获准范围内修正或限定这句话，不抹掉前面的约定，也不临时发明失忆来辩护。若本书本来就在使用不可靠叙述，要先明确那项设计与文本信号，不能把两种情况混作一项。

2. 目的尚未确定的台词：
阿砾对另一个人说：“我从来没答应过与任何人分担任务。”说法仍与约定冲突，但现在它是人物说的话。可能是嘴硬、欺骗，也可能是草稿不一致；孤立一句无法裁定。问他想从这个听者那里争取什么，场景怎样呈现或回应这句话。把“阿砾说了 X”与“X 是事实”分开，不擅自发明秘密动机，也不自动把台词改成实话，或没有依据就判成成功的潜台词。

3. 换策略，不一定是换人设：
另一次后续任务中，作者明确设定开放航路允许阿砾独自按时抵达，他选择独行。这不一定推翻早先答应中继的行为：阻碍不同，他仍可能在乎认可与独立判断。新任务的条件不能反过来让旧场景的北线解禁。若作者真正想改变的是价值选择，应追问哪些事件与回应支持变化，而不是把“独行”或“合作”当作永久人设测试。

审已有书稿时，只请求材料能支持的最小判断：点名当前段落与旧文依据，分开事实和解释，再说明需要局部修正、补清场景过渡，还是交作者决定。找出问题，不等于获得重写人设和后续章节的授权。

保存设计前，可先用普通聊天请求：
只按上面的已确认事实，讨论阿砾的眼前目标、个人动机、惯用办法与面临的选择。每项推断指出材料依据，没有提供的前史保持未知。保留南枝独立的动机和贡献。这次比较都以双方约定中继为结尾，另给一种推进，说明它强调的差别。不新增创伤、秘密能力、晋升或已经完成的送达。
只在回复里交付，不启动写作 skill，不创建或修改文件。这是请求范围，不是工具访问限制的保证。

选定设计后，再明确要求更新相应角色材料与细纲；正文另行点名请求。

en: A concise motive-to-choice explanation grounded in approved material: what the person wants, why it matters, what they try and what changes the available choice. This is an editorial aid, not a new required Oh Story schema.
A separate account of the supporting character’s aim, action and boundary, so the scene does not reduce them to permission for the protagonist.

A proposed sequence with a stated outcome and unresolved author choices. Approved planning can later update the relevant long-form character card and outline; it does not by itself change the chapter-current tracking state.

For a disputed existing passage, an evidence-based distinction between a factual conflict, unresolved speech intent and a change of tactic. State what remains uncertain and the proposed edit scope; do not silently turn an interpretation into character history.

For the next pass, use [character dialogue](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/character-dialogue) to give these motives different conversational actions, and [long-novel continuity](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/long-novel-continuity) to preserve what each person actually knows and has done.
zh: 一份有已确认材料依据的“动机到选择”说明：人物要什么、为什么在乎、先试什么办法，以及什么改变了可选项。这是编辑辅助，不是 Oh Story 新增的强制 schema。
单独说明配角的目标、行动与底线，不把他缩成只负责准许主角的人。
一条说明结果与未决作者选择的候选推进。批准后可以更新相关长篇角色卡与细纲，但规划本身不改变截至当前章的追踪状态。
已有争议段落应给出材料依据，分清事实冲突、尚未确定的说话目的与策略变化；说明仍不确定的部分及拟改范围，不把解释悄悄升格成人物前史。
下一步可用[人物对白指南](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/character-dialogue)把动机变成不同的谈话动作，再用[长篇连续性指南](https://zenstory.ai/oh-story/long-novel-continuity)保存各人确实知道、确实做过的事。

en: Read the chosen action against the character’s information and approved history. If it still feels arbitrary, identify the missing reason or transition rather than adding a diagnostic label or an invented past.

Ask whether a claimed weakness, change or stable conviction actually affects the scene. A filled-out profile and a finished workflow do not prove characterization quality or guarantee consistency across a novel.

The source templates target Chinese web fiction and include optional craft methods alongside workflow instructions. This guide is a selective editorial application, not a promise of a dedicated motivation command, enforced read-only mode or universally required tragic backstory.
zh: 把选择与人物已知信息、批准前史一起读。仍显得突兀时，指出缺少的理由或过渡，不用诊断标签或编造过去来填空。
问被称为弱点、成长或坚定信念的东西，是否真的影响了场景。人设表填满、流程走完，不证明人物写得好，也不保证整本小说都不崩人设。
源模板面向中文网文，同时包含创作技法和流程要求。本指南是有取舍的编辑应用，不承诺专门的动机命令、强制只读模式或人人必需的悲惨前史。
